name: 数字雕塑 / Digital Sculpture
summary: Make type and geometry inhabit a dimensional stage with deliberate light, depth and changes of material.
principles: Treat spatial relationships and material changes as carriers of meaning.
Use a clear focal object, readable words and deliberate camera or object motion.
typography: Prefer solid, confident letterforms with carefully controlled depth or perspective.
Let type participate in the space while keeping a readable statement of the phrase.
composition: Vary close sculptural views, open horizons and relationships between several actors.
Preserve quiet space and a calm bottom caption area.
color: Dark space, cool reflected light and selective warm illumination are starting preferences.
Adapt material and accent colors to the new song rather than copying the demonstration palette.
motion: Change physical relationships: enclosure, release, attraction, transformation, emergence.
Use supplied phrase cues for quick changes of distance, camera angle and scale; let each impact settle rather than jumping randomly.
Calculate object poses and lighting from song time so seeking remains reproducible.
rhythm: Reserve impacts and depth shifts for meaningful musical accents.
Use supplied beat data when available; do not label guessed subdivisions as detected beats.
semantics: Derive the actors and transformations from the new lyrics, not a fixed sequence of cages, spheres or sunrises.
Keep explanatory subtitles visually quieter than the main sculptural type.
transitions: Carry a shape, light direction or depth relationship into the next composition.
Change distance and density as well as color.
avoid: Do not replace each lyric with the same rotating 3D word.
Avoid endless particle wallpaper, unreadable perspective and uncontrolled glow.
The demonstration's phases, props and durations are not a storyboard requirement.

limitations: Authored creative direction. Example observation and review are recorded separately.
